resources.subject: Math
resources.title: Calculus: understanding limits
resources.description: Read graphs and tables to reason about limits, one-sided behavior and points where a function is undefined. Start here before differentiation.

resources.subject: Math
resources.title: Calculus: continuity and discontinuities
resources.description: Review continuity at a point and recognize removable, jump and infinite discontinuities. Connect the value of a function with its limit.

resources.subject: Math
resources.title: Calculus: power, product and quotient rules
resources.description: Choose a differentiation rule for polynomials, products and quotients. Use the worked examples and section exercises to practise selecting a method.

resources.subject: Math
resources.title: Calculus: the chain rule
resources.description: Identify inner and outer functions and include the inner derivative when differentiating a composition. Useful alongside the calculus session recap.

resources.subject: Math
resources.title: Calculus: the Fundamental Theorem
resources.description: Connect antiderivatives with definite integrals and evaluate an integral using its bounds. Compare accumulation with differentiation.

resources.subject: Math
resources.title: Calculus: integration by substitution
resources.description: Recognize an integrand that reverses the chain rule. Practise choosing a substitution and changing variables for indefinite and definite integrals.

resources.subject: Science
resources.title: Biology: cells and microscopy
resources.description: Explore how cells are studied, compare microscopy methods and review cell theory. A starting point for introductory biology.

resources.subject: Science
resources.title: Chemistry: atomic theory and subatomic particles
resources.description: Follow experimental evidence for atomic models and review protons, neutrons, electrons and isotopes.

resources.subject: Science
resources.title: Physics: Newton’s second law
resources.description: Relate net force, mass and acceleration. Practise defining a system before applying Newton’s second law to a problem.

resources.subject: Reading/Writing
resources.title: Writing: build a focused thesis statement
resources.description: Use this guide when planning an analytical, explanatory or argumentative essay. Review the examples, then draft a thesis for your own topic.

resources.subject: Reading/Writing
resources.title: Writing: organize effective paragraphs
resources.description: Review paragraph focus, development and transitions. Use the guide to revise how the ideas in an essay fit together.

resources.subject: Reading/Writing
resources.title: Writing: quotations, paraphrases and summaries
resources.description: Compare three ways of incorporating source material into your writing and review when attribution is needed.

assessmentTemplates.title: Calculus starter: limits and continuity

questions.prompt: A function is undefined at x = 2. Which statement about its limit at 2 is correct?
Which condition is required for continuity at x = a?
choices: f(a) is defined and lim x->a f(x) = f(a)
The derivative at a must be zero
Only the right-hand limit must exist
questions.correct_choice: f(a) is defined and lim x->a f(x) = f(a)

questions.prompt: For x != 3, (x^2 - 9)/(x - 3) simplifies to which expression?
If both one-sided limits at a exist but are different, what happens to the two-sided limit?
